### Given Data:
* Diameter at section 1 ($d_1$) = $20\text{ cm} = 0.2\text{ m}$
* Diameter at section 2 ($d_2$) = $25\text{ cm} = 0.25\text{ m}$
* Velocity at section 1 ($v_1$) = $10\text{ m/s}$

### 1. Discharge ($Q$) at Section 1:
Area at section 1 ($A_1$) = $\frac{\pi}{4} \times d_1^2 = \frac{\pi}{4} \times (0.2)^2 = 0.031416\text{ m}^2$

Discharge ($Q$) = $A_1 \times v_1 = 0.031416 \times 10 = 0.31416\text{ m}^3/\text{sec}$

Converting to liters/sec ($1\text{ m}^3 = 1000\text{ liters}$):
$$Q = 0.31416 \times 1000 = 314.16\text{ L/sec}$$

### 2. Velocity at Section 2 ($v_2$):
Using the Principle of Continuity ($Q = A_1 v_1 = A_2 v_2$):

Area at section 2 ($A_2$) = $\frac{\pi}{4} \times d_2^2 = \frac{\pi}{4} \times (0.25)^2 = 0.049087\text{ m}^2$

$$v_2 = \frac{Q}{A_2} = \frac{0.31416}{0.049087} = 6.40\text{ m/s}$$
proTip: Always convert all units into a consistent system (like SI units in meters) before applying the continuity equation.
